Hi Chloe,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our DPA review we need a clear picture of how data will route between EU and UK tenants and which subprocessors will touch EU personal data. Specifically: SCCs vs UK IDTA applicability, whether any processing will rely on TIAs/DTIAs, and the list of vendor subprocessors + their geographic footprints.

We attached Soteria's questionnaire (two short tabs) — we'd appreciate Redwood's responses so our legal team can confirm the hosting and handover model. Can you also flag any areas where you anticipate needing additional evidence (e.g., SOC2 extracts or localization attestations)?

Best,

Hi Nadia —

Thanks for sending the questionnaire. Attached is a first-pass: Redwood_safeguard_matrix_v1.xlsx with the mapping between (a) SCCs applicability, (b) UK IDTA / UK addendum requirements, and (c) which of our hosted endpoints may require TIA-level controls. High level notes in the matrix: we serve EU traffic from EU regions by default; fallback routing to the UK occurs only when EU capacity is constrained and only to model variants without customer data persistence.

Two quick asks:
- Can you confirm if Soteria requires a strict onshore-only SLA, or if conditional fallback to UK with contractual safeguards is acceptable?
- Please confirm the set of EU legal entities in scope (you listed two in the questionnaire; if there are more, list them).

We will also prepare a subprocessor export (CSV) showing which subprocessors process token-level telemetry vs platform-level metrics — that should help your team decide whether further attestations are required.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood to send subprocessor_map_export.csv and a short evidence bundle to the Drive link.
2) Internal review (Redwood legal + infra) — Kimberley/Kim to confirm any technical mitigations.
3) Final DPA/DocuSign packet to Soteria legal.

I've looped in Kimberly and Laura to confirm timelines and signoff owners. If that plan works I'll post the Drive link and DocuSign draft later today.

Thanks,

Chloe / Nadia —

Quick technical clarity from infra ops: for Soteria's expected workload (sequence lengths + throughput) the default EU cluster will handle 99.6% of requests. Fallback to UK is a staged policy we can enable per-customer; when enabled the routing will only send inference payloads to a UK-only model pool that has no persistent customer KV storage. That means: no customer-request data is written to long-term stores in the UK path (ephemeral caches only).

On evidence: we can provide:
- SOC2 summary extract + assertion of control coverage (scope: serving runtime, caching)
- Per-subprocessor data access scoping (we'll label token-level vs telemetry)
- A terse TIA appendix for UK fallback that outlines contractual safeguards (encryption in transit, access controls, logging retention)

I can prepare the subprocessor CSV and a one-page TIA appendix draft. ETA: EOD tomorrow for the CSV; TIA appendix by Fri COB.

Kimberly Park
Director, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference
